The US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) has developed and presented a new plan for the conquest of outer space for the coming decades.

In addition to some key Earth-orbiting missions, the agency is planning the first manned space missions beyond Earth space in more than 40 years, first returning a man to the Moon and then sending him to Mars.

The agency has developed a new plan in accordance with the requirements put forward by the current administration of US President Donald Trump - to return the country to leadership in the space sector.

According to the 21-page document released by the agency, NASA has set itself five key objectives, the solution of which will not only restore the country's leadership in space, but also prepare the basis for more ambitious tasks in deep space exploration.

Among them: active support of the private space sector and more active international cooperation, preparation for further development of near-Earth and cislunar space, support for scientific discoveries, as well as the characterization of lunar resources during a series of robotic missions to the satellite of our planet, the return of American astronauts to the surface of the Moon with the prospect of permanent presence on it, as well as the development and implementation of manned flights to Mars and other destinations.
NASA's plan to send a man to the Moon and Mars is designed for 20 years, but the first landing is planned to be carried out in 10 years.

At the same time, the experts in the published document took into account all force majeure situations and a possible change in the timing if problems arise at one or another stage of the implementation of the overall strategy.

In low-Earth orbit operations, NASA is about to move away from the current model of space exploration, in which the US government (which is essentially the main customer of space launches) takes an active part, and turn towards private commercial enterprises.
In short, NASA is about to move from direct government and funding to commercial partnerships and services, as well as greater international cooperation.
The agency wants to apply a similar approach to the International Space Station after 2025.
Recall that support for the station will continue until at least 2024.

All this time, NASA plans to use the station as a platform for testing new technologies in robotics, communications, medicine, agriculture and other areas that will be required for the implementation of the further part of the deep space exploration program.
At the same time, the ISS will have to play a key role for the agency in NASA's transition to a more commercial focus on low-Earth orbit services.

In particular, we are talking about launching new private compact satellites (cubesats) from the station, using it as a research platform in non-governmental missions, and also, possibly, for a partial restructuring of the American segment into a space tourist hotel.
An important role in the implementation of this part of the plan will be assigned to the new Space Launch System (SLS) launch vehicle and the Orion multipurpose spacecraft.
The first test launch of the Orion spacecraft (Exploration Mission-1) in unmanned mode is scheduled for 2020.
During this mission, the device is planned to be sent around the moon and returned back to Earth.
It is planned to follow Exploration Mission-2, scheduled for 2023.
Within its framework, the agency will send a team of astronauts around the moon.
The first landing on the lunar surface with the successful completion of the Exploration Mission-2 mission will be carried out no earlier than the end of the 2020s.

Another important step in the development of the moon will be the construction of the Gateway lunar orbital station, which will allow the United States to consolidate its permanent presence in the circumlunar space.
The station is planned to be used as a scientific laboratory for studying the Moon, as well as the effects of microgravity and radiation on living organisms.
The results of this work will form the basis of preparations for further exploration of deep space, in particular Mars.
The station itself, in turn, in the future will become a transit point for flights to Mars and other bodies of the solar system.
The first element of the station is planned to be laid in 2022.
The first manned mission to Mars will happen no earlier than the 2030s.
The main work on preparing for a flight to Mars is planned to begin after receiving the results of the Mars 2020 mission, during which a new rover will be sent to the Red Planet.
The new apparatus will not only search for life on our planetary neighbor, but also explore the possibilities of using local resources by future colonists in the construction of a permanent habitat.

An important aspect in the preparation of manned flights to Mars will be the development of robotic missions to the Red Planet, which will expand the scientific and technical knowledge that will be obtained in the course of missions to explore the Moon.

According to the document presented by NASA, an important part of the plan for the development of Mars will be the creation of orbital infrastructure, which will be used to conduct new missions in the orbit of the planet, as well as landings on the surface of Mars.
The agency commissioned the company to develop a concept document for the Mars Base Camp orbital station, which in the future will be used in a similar way to the lunar Gateway station.
It is planned to place its own landing rover on board the station, with the help of which missions will be carried out on the Red Planet.
